content: The use of radiotherapy has been explored as a treatment option for keloid scars, aiming to reduce their size and prevent recurrence after surgical excision. Corticosteroids, particularly intralesional injections, are commonly employed to manage keloid scars by suppressing inflammation and fibroblast activity, which are key contributors to excessive collagen deposition. Radiotherapy is typically administered in low doses and is most effective when applied immediately after surgical removal of the keloid tissue. Corticosteroid therapy, on the other hand, can be used as a standalone treatment or in combination with other modalities, such as surgery or radiotherapy, to enhance therapeutic outcomes. Both approaches target the pathological processes underlying keloid formation, but their efficacy and safety profiles may vary depending on individual patient factors and the characteristics of the keloid.
